newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Queen Elizabeth portrait comes down at HK barracks.
newsitem.headline: Queen Elizabeth portrait comes down at HK barracks.

text.p: British forces removed portraits of Queen Elizabeth from their Hong Kong headquarters barracks on Monday in preparation for the territory's handover to China at midnight on June 30.
The monarch is commander-in-chief of the British military whose Hong Kong facilities are being turned over to the People's Liberation Army.
Larger-than-lifesize photographic portraits of the queen and her husband, the Duke of Edinburgh, were taken from the officers' mess and presented to the British Trade Commission.
The commission will become the office of the British Consul General in Hong Kong after the handover ends 156 years of colonial rule.
"Every British officers' mess in the world has portraits of the Queen and the Duke," explained Captain Sara Wood, a British forces spokeswoman.
"Taking these down was a part of the process of our preparing to leave Hong Kong. We were just happy to find a fitting home for them."
Foreshadowing a military shutdown, the two portraits were removed without ceremony by forces wearing white tropical kit of shirts, shorts and knee-high socks.
The Prince of Wales barracks from which the portraits were removed is one of a number of British forces bases scheduled to be handed over to the PLA when Hong Kong reverts to China.
Civilian authorities have already been busy removing royal insignia like the crown, from government buiildings and post boxes.
